title: Why You Shouldn’t Stay Late After School
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that, for most teachers, staying late after school to plan and prepare is a mistake, distinguishing those who genuinely enjoy the extra hours from those who feel trapped by them. He lists four reasons staying late backfires: mental sharpness declines after a full day, denying daily decompression is a primary driver of teacher stress, afternoons are full of unavoidable distractions (parents, colleagues, former students), and chronic overwork leads to burnout that undermines patience and effectiveness. His proposed alternative is waking up earlier to do planning before school, when the mind is fresher and distractions are fewer, claiming that even fifteen extra morning minutes can save a full half hour of afternoon work.
points: Distinguishes teachers who genuinely choose to stay late (a preference) from those who feel they must, despite the stress it causes.
After a full day of teaching, mental sharpness declines, making after-school work take longer than necessary.
Denying the need to decompress after school is a primary driver of teacher stress and eventual burnout.
Afternoons are full of unavoidable distractions—parents, colleagues, former students—that fragment planning time.
Recommended alternative: wake up 15 extra minutes earlier to do focused planning before school, potentially saving a full half hour in the afternoon.
quotes: There are those rare teachers, perhaps one or two at every school site, who pride themselves with how late they stay after school.
But the truth is, for most teachers, staying late is a mistake.
After a long day of teaching, a long day on your feet talking, making decisions, and managing your classroom, your mind won’t be nearly as sharp and clear as it was when you arrived in the morning.
Denying this need day after day will tear you up inside and cause a great amount of stress.
To be the best teacher you can be for your students, to have patience, calmness, and likability, to have spot-on classroom management and a passion for teaching, you must get away from it.
If you can carve out an extra fifteen minutes, just fifteen minutes, you'll save yourself a half hour in the afternoon.
